pr.title: Prepare selective server, Android and iOS releases
pr.body:
## Summary

Maintainers currently decide and run server, native and OTA releases separately, which makes unnecessary builds and uncertain retries difficult to avoid. This prepares one manual **Release changed artifacts** entrypoint that compares immutable inputs with each artifact's last verified success, proposes versions and runs only the required existing workers.

The plan preserves Android phone/Wear allocation, exact-candidate CI, signed tags and image receipts. It adds independent iOS build allocation and IPA verification, compatible per-runtime OTA, and durable recovery without blindly repeating uncertain provider requests. Backend/project/profile settings are supplied externally at build time. iOS upload inputs are prepared separately; TestFlight processing and production rollout are not claimed.

Refs #447. **Review order: PR441, then this child.** Actual target: `mchartier/release-entrypoints-recovery` at `cd8932b2`; source parent: `0c26cea`; ultimate target: `master` at `9dc0739`. PR441 is preserved. Managed-hosted PR450 remains a separate integration dependency; its UI is not imported here.

## Test plan and behavior evidence

This is non-UI release tooling. The evidence is [actual synthetic CLI/JSON plans, worker arguments and state transitions](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/blob/80703680c484c534bcfa0f7ee18760870d2acc6f/behavior.json), with [reproduction and full evidence](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/blob/80703680c484c534bcfa0f7ee18760870d2acc6f/README.md).

| Starting state and action | Expected and observed |
| --- | --- |
| All verified artifact inputs match; execute the plan | No stages and zero journal/candidate/provider writes. |
| Change only server, either native platform, or either compatible bundle | Select only the corresponding stage; OTA retains the installed native runtime. |
| Change server and both native inputs | Allocate paired Android and independent iOS versions, then run server last through its original candidate/image gates. |
| Lose a provider response, then retry twice | Retain intent, reconcile one operation and reuse its verified result; one provider start total. |
| Retry OTA with an empty provider inventory | Reject another publication. Changed native/configuration/export/channel identities also reject in maintained regressions. |
| Prepare iOS delivery | Build arguments freeze existing credentials; upload arguments select an exact verified store build. Neither command was executed against a provider. |

Maintained fixtures additionally cover stale source, missing/failed CI, incompatible OTA, partial completion, conflicting receipts, concurrency and interrupted cleanup with retained tombstones/readback.

## Supporting checks and limitations

Release tests: **272 passed, 2 skipped**; native-release: **273 passed**. Operations, Wear-emulator unit and deployment tests passed, as did release configuration checks. Final affected workflow/snapshot and receipt-policy tests passed after the full suites.

Raw actionlint 1.7.12 is **not clean**: 61 inherited diagnostics and seven added diagnostics concern documented GitHub Cloud features absent from its schema. [Exact comparison and primary-source compatibility evidence](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/blob/80703680c484c534bcfa0f7ee18760870d2acc6f/actionlint-compatibility.json) retain the unfiltered results; no broad suppression was added.

Source: `53de4b70`. The [complete published scope](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/blob/ced19a3b2b32f67aa5fdf1abea2b7b9342326a03/final-scope.json) binds three focused commits, 86 files, source parent and current ultimate master `9dc0739`; `4cbcbc7` is the source merge-base. Detailed logs remain on a separate nonmerged evidence ref.

Twenty-six affected tests pass at this head; the earlier behavior evidence remains applicable after removal of six unused exports ([impact assessment](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/blob/ced19a3b2b32f67aa5fdf1abea2b7b9342326a03/final-applicability.json)). All five hosted workflows passed at this unchanged head against source parent `0c26cea`: Lint, Tests, Builds (including Android debug and iOS simulator compilation), Production Container Scan, and Database Upgrade classification; migration jobs were correctly skipped. The [actual-target impact check](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/blob/09cd0416e305b7e4e3c0ea0791cf5e34b6e24146/parent-impact.json) verifies conflict-free documentation integration, 25 local links and unchanged commands. Its byte-identical child patch preserves existing behavior/test applicability; no new hosted run against `cd8932b2` is claimed. The configured Codex review [refused solely for review quota](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/pull/452#issuecomment-6070337167); no bot review is claimed or retried. Independent QA and human readiness remain with the coordinator. No actual release, paid build, credential setup, provider upload/publication, deployment or device installation occurred. Real macOS IPA/provider validation and native-device checks remain unrun.

Restore saved targets in completed-day Daily Balance (#436)

## Summary

Completed days can show “Saved target unavailable” even when their
calorie target was saved: Daily Balance reads a single-day response that
drops the comparison returned by the calendar. This change returns the
validated saved comparison in day reads and phone/watch completion
acknowledgements, including their sync payloads. Existing snapshots
retain their original target; missing legacy history remains
unavailable.

Closes #435. Targets `master`; no unmerged dependency. No data repair,
migration or current-target substitution.

## Test plan and behavior evidence

| Scenario | Expected and observed |
| --- | --- |
| Read a completed day with 1,800 kcal intake and a saved 2,000 target |
The actual changed serializer and app show **200 kcal remaining**; the
actual base shows unavailable. |
| Complete today, refetch and reload while the current plan differs |
Three maintained browser cases pass, including switching from the
current 2,100 target to saved 2,000 and retaining it after reload.
Backend route tests verify acknowledgement, read and sync consistency. |
| Missing legacy snapshot or older payload without the optional field |
Remains unavailable after reload. Backend tests also preserve snapshots
through goal changes/recompletion and reject partial snapshots and
invalid totals. |

### Before / After

Actual base `4cbcbc74` → captured source `3ac32ffa`. Current head
`d94a34d0` only adds corrected API description/generated comments;
runtime behavior and captures are unchanged. Independently built Windows
Chrome apps, identical synthetic fixtures and 390×844 viewport; these
are browser captures, not physical-device evidence. API fixtures below
are generated by each revision's actual serializer. [Exact
source/build/fixture provenance and
hashes](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/blob/7dd85c054275e336e1c42ff3b85ec6442d426c67/README.md).

**Valid saved target: the day becomes comparable again.**

unavailable](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/7dd85c054275e336e1c42ff3b85ec6442d426c67/before-valid.png)
| ![After: 200 kcal
remaining](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/7dd85c054275e336e1c42ff3b85ec6442d426c67/after-valid.png)
|

**Missing snapshot: historical values are not invented.**

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: missing
snapshot](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/7dd85c054275e336e1c42ff3b85ec6442d426c67/before-missing.png)
| ![After: still
unavailable](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/7dd85c054275e336e1c42ff3b85ec6442d426c67/after-missing.png)
|

## Supporting checks and limitations

Local validation passed: 764 backend tests, 53 focused client tests,
backend typecheck, independent baseline/current web builds, three
browser regressions and four capture cases. Evidence is retained outside
the product history; the PR has two scoped commits and ten files,
including the required API description/generated mirror.

No live database, user OTA or physical-device run. Actual deployed
versions and the affected records' snapshot state remain unverified.
Unrelated transient PWA notices were suppressed consistently during
capture. GitHub-page rendering verification is waived; genuine
pixel/provenance and independent QA requirements remain. [Bot review was
quota-refused](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/pull/436#issuecomment-6029479109)
on the captured source; no completed bot review is claimed. Independent
QA remains required.

issue.title: Unify selective releases and prepare iOS/TestFlight delivery

labels.description: Needs value, scope, acceptance criteria or authorization before agent dispatch.

issue.body:
## Problem

Releasing Calibrate currently requires separate server, native and OTA decisions and commands. The user wants one manually invoked GitHub Action to manage versions, determine which artifacts changed, and prepare Android and iOS/TestFlight delivery before production. Published Little Say PR42 is the fixed planner/retirement design reference, not permission to execute release operations.

## Requirements and acceptance

- Provide one manual release entrypoint that plans server image, Android/iOS native build and compatible OTA work from an exact protected source revision. Automatic change detection compares each artifact/profile/platform with its last successful compatible result, not merely the last release tag.
- Manage versions and platform build numbers consistently. Preserve candidate CI/review gates and exact-source verification; no publishing from ordinary merges. Explicit plans, no-change results and validation failures must be readable.
- Preserve successful artifact identities across partial failures and retries; reconcile uncertain provider responses, reject conflicting receipts and avoid duplicate version allocation, builds, images or submissions. Test recovery and idempotency using fixtures/mocks.
- Prepare iOS/TestFlight and Android distribution code/configuration alongside native/OTA compatibility and runtime fingerprints. Publication, store rollout, server deployment and device uptake remain distinct.
- Keep personal/account/Expo-project/signing configuration out of the public repository, logs and artifacts. Use documented secret/environment inputs and redaction where appropriate; client backend configuration necessarily shipped in a bundle is observable and must not be described as secret.
- Honor managed-first build-time backend targeting from [the product amendment](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/issues/405#issuecomment-6049386828). An Expo channel alone must not be assumed to set a backend URL.
- This task authorizes source/configuration/docs/tests and a draft PR with independent QA only. No actual release, image/OTA publication, cloud build spend, Apple/Play upload or submission, signing/credential setup, merge or deployment.

## Implementation plan

Reconcile current master, the existing release-entrypoint PR441 and published Little Say PR42. Prefer a distinct dependent PR pinned to PR441 only if its changes are needed; otherwise use reverified master. Preserve PR441 and coordinate ownership before overlapping edits.

Build an immutable selective-artifact plan using each platform/profile’s last verified successful receipt. Reuse Calibrate’s existing publication workers, exact-source CI and image/signing trust verification. Bind endpoint, EAS project, environment, channel, runtime/native fingerprint and source in build/export/OTA receipts. Current EAS profiles select preview/production separately from the update header; validate agreement rather than assume channel names choose endpoints.

Generalize native-internal-release.mjs instance constants through validated external configuration, coordinating that helper and release docs with #438. Extend iOS version/store build and submission preparation without disrupting Android phone/Wear allocation. Existing iOS bundle/simulator configuration is not TestFlight readiness. Verify current primary Expo/Apple requirements; keep account/signing inputs external and exact-build selection explicit.

Use Little Say PR42’s published fixed retirement/tombstone and interrupted-run reconciliation design; do not copy its pre-fix cleanup behavior. Test no-change, individual/combined artifacts, incompatible OTA, stale candidates, missing CI, partial success, lost responses and retries using fixtures. Preparation needs no live credentials; provider operations remain unperformed.

[Original issue requirements and plan](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/issues/447#issuecomment-6065173979) remain preserved.

## Implementing Codex task

Current preparation owner: verified task ID `01a11cd8-3e02-703c-831c-fdc6176d7028`. The prior release-entrypoint owner and PR441 remain preserved.

## Implementing PR

[PR452 — Prepare selective server, Android and iOS releases](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/pull/452), a draft child of preserved [PR441](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/pull/441). This association is nonclosing and covers preparation only; no release or provider execution is implied.

+# Selective release preparation
+
+`Release changed artifacts` is the manual entrypoint for maintainers of the
+managed Calibrate service. Its default **plan only** mode reports which server,
+Android, iOS and compatible OTA artifacts differ from their last verified success.
+Merging application code does not invoke this workflow. This guide describes
+prepared automation; it is not evidence that a release or provider operation ran.
+
+## Plan and execute
+
+Select protected `master`, a build profile (`internal` or `production`), and a
+server version bump. Leave **plan only** enabled to inspect the JSON summary.
+The plan reports exact source and configuration digests, selected stages, reasons
+and proposed versions. A no-change plan writes no journal, candidate or provider
+request. The Android Play Console acknowledgement is required only when the
+plan selects the existing paired Android upload worker.
+
+After reviewing the plan and existing provider configuration, an authorized
+operator can dispatch again with **plan only** disabled. This creates a fresh
+plan at that exact source; the protected handler compares its read-only and
+execution digests before writes. It verifies selected workflow availability and
+allocation constraints before preparing metadata. Native metadata changes use
+one exact candidate with the maintained base/head CI and tree guards. GitHub may
+require a human to approve CI on a bot-created candidate PR; missing or failed
+CI leaves that candidate recoverable and prevents provider dispatch.
+
+Selected native and OTA stages finish before the separate server handoff. That
+handoff retains the existing server-only candidate and image-receipt verifier.
+Selective server publication does not implicitly deploy or launch another OTA
+publication. Existing manual server recovery and local native build options
+remain available.
+
+## External build configuration
+
+No production domain is selected in source. The operator supplies an explicit,
+credential-free HTTPS origin through `CALIBRATE_NATIVE_SERVER_URL` for production
+or `CALIBRATE_INTERNAL_SERVER_URL` for internal builds. New unified workflows read
+the EAS project UUID from masked `CALIBRATE_EAS_PROJECT_ID` configuration, including
+the paired Android worker. The separate legacy OTA entrypoint retains its public
+repository-variable input of the same name; keep that value identical if it is
+still used. Unified workflows use the secret form to keep project settings out
+of workflow logs.
+
+The selected EAS environment must agree with all three values:
+
+| Build profile | EAS environment | Update channel |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `internal` | `preview` | `internal` |
+| `production` | `production` | `production` |
+
+The EAS environment supplies `EXPO_PUBLIC_CALIBRATE_SERVER_URL`,
+`EXPO_PUBLIC_EAS_PROJECT_ID` and `EXPO_UPDATES_CHANNEL`. A channel selects an update
+stream; it does **not** select a backend URL. The environment, endpoint, project,
+profile, source and native fingerprint are bound together. A mismatch rejects
+the build/export. Existing channel mappings must contain one active branch;
+the worker never creates or remaps a channel or continues through a rollout.
+OTA publication retains the existing production/preview GitHub environment gate.
+
+Backend targeting is build-time only. These endpoint/project values are embedded
+in clients and are observable. They are not credentials. Temporary OTA exports
+necessarily contain the public configuration and bundle; only their digests and
+verified result identities enter durable release receipts. Raw EAS environment
+contents, account names, Apple team settings and signing inputs are not retained
+in those receipts. The managed-hosted application behavior is maintained by the
+separate fixed-target client change; this tooling adds no runtime server picker.
+
+Existing Expo authentication remains `EXPO_TOKEN`. Existing Apple team identity
+is supplied as `APPLE_TEAM_ID`; account ownership, where needed locally, uses
+`EAS_ACCOUNT`. Do not commit provider credentials or personal project settings.
+This preparation neither creates credentials nor provisions a service.
+
+## Native versions and iOS delivery
+
+Android retains the paired phone/Wear allocation, signed native tags, original
+image/signing trust policy and separated Play submission stages. An Android
+selection still uses the existing internal-upload worker; production rollout
+is a separate operator decision. Local `native:release`, retry and skip-build
+options remain supported.
+
+iOS uses `shared/ios-release.json` independently of Android's paired counters.
+The candidate advances the iOS version, build number and maintained diagnostic
+mirrors together. Native runtime identity is `ios-VERSION-BUILDNUMBER`; compatible
+OTA exports retain the installed runtime rather than allocating another build.
+The EAS CLI is locked to 22.4.0 and build requests freeze existing credentials.
+Builds never automatically submit.
+
+The stages have distinct outcomes:
+
+1. **Build:** EAS produces an IPA. A separate macOS verifier downloads the exact
+   bytes and checks the signature, provisioning, bundle identity, version, build
+   number, runtime, project, channel and backend configuration. Only its attested
+   receipt can advance the native baseline.
+2. **Upload:** `iosSubmitRequest` prepares an explicit `eas submit --id BUILD_ID`
+   request and external `ascAppId` configuration for an independently verified
+   store build. It forbids latest/simulator/ad-hoc selection and automatic
+   TestFlight setup. This pure preparation helper does not execute submission.
+3. **TestFlight processing:** Apple processes an uploaded build before it becomes
+   available. Export-compliance information and testing eligibility remain
+   App Store Connect concerns; upload success is not processing success.
+4. **Production rollout:** App Review and App Store release remain separate human
+   operations. Neither an IPA nor an upload receipt proves a production release.
+
+Apple's requirements effective April 28, 2026 require iOS uploads built with
+Xcode 26 or later and the iOS 26 SDK or later. The selected named EAS image uses
+Xcode 26.6; the downloaded IPA verifier checks its SDK metadata too. See
+[Apple's requirements](https://developer.apple.com/news/upcoming-requirements/),
+[Expo iOS build infrastructure](https://docs.expo.dev/build-reference/infrastructure/),
+[EAS iOS submission](https://docs.expo.dev/submit/ios/) and
+[TestFlight delivery](https://docs.expo.dev/submit/testflight/).
+
+## Recovery and retirement
+
+Each manual handler owns an append-only draft-release journal. It retains the
+original plan, exact candidate, provider intent and verified per-stage receipts.
+These are operational records, not completed release announcements. One unresolved
+journal blocks a new allocation across profiles.
+
+Rerun the retained failed worker/handler after resolving its explicit obstacle;
+do not dispatch a replacement release to escape an uncertain result. Successful
+stages are reverified and reused. Lost responses require a complete provider
+inventory and a unique matching operation. An empty inventory after interruption,
+multiple matches, changed export bytes or a moved channel blocks another request.
+Worker failure may include partial publication and is never proof of absence.
+
+OTA publication has a separate durable intent containing the exact export and
+channel digests. The writer has no Expo token; the source-free publisher has no
+GitHub content-write permission. The publisher checks delivered manifest and asset
+bytes before attesting success. Historical receipts remain usable after temporary
+workflow artifacts expire, subject to current protected signer policy. The
+historical iOS/selective-OTA policy file is
+`.github/ios-release-attestation-trusted-workflow-shas`; explicit revocation wins.
+
+Automatic retirement is restricted to proven terminal, unpublished candidates
+with complete all-attempt job evidence and no provider intent. It records a
+durable tombstone, retains original assets, closes only the verified unmerged
+candidate and reads back cleanup. Retryable, merged, partial, unknown or uncertain
+publication states remain recoverable. Interrupted cleanup resumes from the
+tombstone and cannot silently discard the original identities.
+
+## Safe validation
+
+`npm run test:release` and `npm run test:native-release` exercise synthetic plans,
+worker arguments, byte-bound receipts, CI rejection, interruption, retries and
+cleanup. They do not invoke live release workflows or providers. Native device
+testing, a real EAS build, macOS IPA inspection against a real provider artifact,
+Apple upload/processing and production rollout remain separate unperformed
+operator validation. Use the PR's retained evidence for the exact tested revision
+and current CI/review state.
